items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, trade and demand design form); Claude (written into POPULATION, MARKETS, SUPPLY, PRODUCTION); restored 2026-09-23 by Ben's ruling on BL-1066
items.title: Goods pools are keyed per (corp, market), so a same-body haul delivers and sells where it arrives
items.design:
RESTORED 2026-09-23 (Ben, BL-1066 form: "Restore BL-1003 pools per market"). It is the structural cause of BL-1066 (the player cannot build): on the shipped home body (255 markets) a build draws from its TILE's market, but wants, fills, pools and auto-surplus book at the corp's representative market, and a same-body convoy credits the seller's own (corp, body) pool. So steel at 10x base price at a build market induced nothing, and a market no steel seller calls home is empty forever. Measured: the player's base at tile (45,97), market 56211, drew 0 steel for 100 ticks while 558 steel sat in 5 of 255 markets. PRODUCTION.md § Stockpile and output flow already states the rule; the prose below is 2026-09-15 and its file:line anchors predate sprint 45 — re-read before trusting them. BL-1006 (far trade reading), its old prerequisite, is complete. The re-pin of every world digest this moves is a re-bless and is Ben's to authorise; it should ride sprint 46's single re-bless with BL-1049.

--- THE ORIGINAL ITEM (2026-09-15) ---
SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-15, form: pools per market over a consignment). PRODUCTION.md § Stockpile and output flow owns it; MARKETS.md § Market centres and seeding and SUPPLY.md § Convoy entity amended.

DEFECT IT FIXES (found 2026-09-15): pools are keyed (corp, body) (world.hpp:272, :701-703); commit_convoy debits pool_for(corp, src_body) (supply_system.cpp:660) and arrival credits pool_for(corp, dest_body) (:182-183) — the same pool on one body — and auto-surplus then sells through market_for_corp_on_body, the lowest-id building's market (market_clearing.cpp:206-221). Every same-body market-to-market haul paid haulage and sold back at home. haulage_measure's 1614 same-body hauls measured dispatch, never trade.

THE RULE: a building's output enters the pool of market_for_tile(building tile); its inputs draw that pool plus that market's inventory; wants, purchases, auto-surplus, standing orders and the running remainder key (corp, market). A body with no market keeps one body-level pool until its first building spawns one. Labour pools stay (corp, body).

COSTS, STATED: save format (save_game_version moves, round-trip assertion owed per NR-708); state_hash folds the new key in sorted order; a roster straddling a catchment line now needs hauls, so the landscape search must score it — measure how many generated firms straddle before and after.

DONE WHEN: a harness hauls a good between two markets on one body and the goods sell at the destination price; world_determinism bit-identical across runs; save round-trips pools; the landscape search winner still validates.

CARRIED 2026-09-24: sprint 46 closed early; unscheduled pending the sprint 47 cut.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-18, sprint 45 elicitation); Claude (item text, from a five-lane engine read with an adversarial check per lane)
items.title: A captured capital's treasury is stranded, where the design says a conqueror takes the stores standing in the seat
items.design:
FITTED TO SPRINT 46 (Ben, 2026-09-23: fit the strays into 46 or drop them — the focus is wiring the generation into the game). A nation's opening treasury IS what crosses into play (NATION_GENERATION.md § Pass 7, and NR-912 re-read its rate on the shipped world), so a chest stranded on a captured capital is a wrong number in the campaign, not a fidelity nit.

CONTINUITY PASS (Ben, 2026-09-18): held for the continuity pass run after each generation round is done — this one after Industrialisation — not built mid-sprint.

FOUND 2026-09-18 by the sprint 45 engine read (industry-points lane, checked). When a capital falls the loser re-seats at held.front() and the treasury stays on the captured region (history_sim.cpp:3784-3806). The conqueror's upkeep reads only regions[q.capital].treasury, and consolidation fires once, at the span's start (cpp:886, :902-916), so a captured treasury is neither the loser's nor the winner's — it is stranded. EXPLORATION.md's located-stock rule says a conqueror who takes the seat takes the stores standing in it.

NOT ON SPRINT 45's RE-BLESS (Ben, 2026-09-18, elicitation: offered as a rider, not taken). Beat 1's industry points do not inherit the defect, because they are read per region at the handoff. Fix: fold a captured seat's treasury into the conqueror's capital at capture (or state that it stays and why), then measure; it moves shipped worlds.

items.author: Claude (BL-1050's own prose, unbuilt; 2026-09-20)
items.title: A lint holds the byte-identical-replay rule: every unordered store on world is faithful, and no reader walks one into arithmetic
items.design:
FITTED TO SPRINT 46 (Ben, 2026-09-23). It guards the byte-identical-replay rule that sprint 45 had to fix by hand in BL-1050 — seven readers found one at a time, at the cost of a whole item and part of a re-bless. Wiring the generation into the game means saving and loading it, so the rule is load-bearing for 46, and a lint is what keeps it from rotting again.

CONTINUITY PASS. BL-1050's prose asks for it and its R1-R7 do not require it, so it was not built with the item (lane report, 2026-09-20). The rule (TECH_FOUNDATIONS.md ~104-111: a loaded world replays byte for byte, and so does a copy) is today held by six hand-fixed readers and one tripwire type; nothing stops the seventh being written. THE WORK: a check that fails when a store on `world` that should be faithful_unordered_map is a plain unordered_map, and when a reader walks an unordered store into a float sum, a strict-inequality tie-break or a write order — a source scan is acceptable if it names what it cannot see. Run it in the verify suite. DONE WHEN: it fails on a deliberately reverted reader (BL-1050's own five make the fixtures) and passes on main.

items.author: Claude (BL-1034 cold review, carried again by BL-1050 and its review, 2026-09-20)
items.title: A throw inside a landscape-search worker reaches std::terminate and its message is dropped
items.design:
FITTED TO SPRINT 46 (Ben, 2026-09-23). The faithful_unordered_map throw is the tripwire the replay rule stands on, and it fires inside the landscape search every new game runs — a crash there currently reaches std::terminate with its message lost, which is a debugging hole in the exact path 46 is wiring.

CONTINUITY PASS. FOUND by BL-1034 (world copies diverge) cold review, carried unbuilt through BL-1050 and named again by its review (2026-09-20). faithful_unordered_map throws a logic_error when a copy cannot keep its source order — the tripwire the byte-identical-replay rule stands on. Thrown inside a landscape-search worker thread it reaches std::terminate, and the handler (main.cpp ~l.383) drops the message, so the one diagnostic the tripwire exists to print is exactly what is lost. THE WORK: catch in the worker and carry the message to the joining thread (or set a failure slot the search reports), so a tripwire throw names the store and the site. DONE WHEN: a deliberately unfaithful copy inside a worker prints its message and fails the run, rather than terminating silently.

items.author: Claude (found running BL-1044's owed ctest pass, 2026-09-22)
items.title: The CTest tier links what its harnesses now use: a family of Debug targets has been unbuildable since the harnesses adopted the app-order build
items.design:
FOUND 2026-09-22 running BL-1044's owed ctest pass. `nmake all` stops at the first failing target, so the suite reads as "Not Run" rather than as a broken build, and the breakage hid.

WHAT IS BROKEN. Every harness that builds its world in APP ORDER goes through tools/verify/harness_params.hpp, which includes scripting/lua_state.hpp and calls build_app_base_world — so it needs lua54 AND the Lua TUs the Lua-free world superset excludes (world_gen_config.cpp, works_registry.cpp, recipe_registry.cpp, tech_tree.cpp). The CMake targets name those by hand, one target at a time, and the ones written before harness_params spread do not. Measured tonight, building all 157 CTest targets by name: player_seed_sweep failed on LNK2019 world_gen_config::load_from_lua / works_registry::load_from_lua (fixed at ee7ef3c3, which restored the player_seed_sweep_guard row — the row that now carries the one-player invariant, S7); campaign_lapse, chain_conversion_probe, convoy_cargo_census and others fail on LNK2019 lua_close / luaL_unref, i.e. they do not link lua54 at all. battle_engagement_harness is a separate, older break (a torn-out mercenary symbol, 2026-08-30).

THE WORK. Take the failing list from the overnight build (scratchpad overnight3/build_failures.txt, or rebuild by name to regenerate it); for each, add lua54 and whichever Lua TUs it pulls, or move it onto a shared helper so the list stops being hand-kept — the hand-kept list is the defect, and DEVELOPMENT_PRACTICES.md § A harness must build the world the application builds is what keeps growing it. Then run the suite and record which rows breach the 60 s default now that the span runs by default (BL-1044: the budget row's generation is a median 53.3 s in Release).

DONE WHEN. Every CTest target builds by name, `ctest --test-dir build` runs every row rather than reporting Not Run, and the rows that legitimately exceed 60 s carry a raised timeout with the reason.

THE LIST, measured 2026-09-22 by building all 157 CTest test names (14 stops, three classes). (a) DOES NOT LINK LUA (LNK2019 lua_close / luaL_unref), 9: campaign_lapse, chain_conversion_probe, convoy_cargo_census, industrialisation_sim_harness, exploration_sweep, history_sweep, material_floor, stockpile_budget_check, world_copy_determinism. (b) DOES NOT COMPILE against the current headers, 3: whole_firm_buyout and battle_engagement_harness read world::mercenary_contracts, retired by NR-885 on 2026-09-17; nation_scorer_harness fails on a missing type. Those are stale harnesses, not a link list — each is a decision to re-point or retire. (c) NOT A TARGET, 1: player_seed_sweep_guard is a ctest TEST name whose target is player_seed_sweep (fixed at ee7ef3c3); the build loop took test names, so a name that is not a target reads as a stop.

items.author: Claude (found running BL-1044's owed visual suite, 2026-09-23)
items.title: The player's own construction does not complete on the shipped world: a military base sits unfinished for 100 ticks with 70,000 credits in hand
items.design:
DIAGNOSED 2026-09-23 (Release --verify probes with a temporary run_construction trace; probes and patch in that session's scratchpad). Capacity is NOT the stall: BL-709 floors capacity coverage at 1/max_stretch, so it only stretches. The stall is MATERIALS, in three layers:

(1) WRONG MARKET, AND NOTHING CAN REFILL IT. The fixture's build_first_valid placed at raster-first tile (45,97), market 56211: 0 steel for 100 ticks, demand there 0.00 — the build's want booked at the corp's representative market, not the draw market. Steel existed on the body (558 units) but in 5 of 255 markets, and a same-body convoy lands in the seller's own (corp, body) pool. Structural cause, owned by BL-1003 (pools per market).

(2) THE SITE MULTIPLIER DRAWS MORE THAN WAS PRICED. The per-tick draw is cost/build_duration_ticks per unit of progress, but ticks_remaining carries BL-323's site multiplier, so a hard site draws cost x multiplier while construct_building's affordability gate priced the authored cost. Placed next to home (market 56166, 36.5 steel), the 35-steel base drew 36.5, stalled at 4.1 of 5+ progress units and never finished.

(3) ZERO CONSTRUCTION CAPACITY. 0 construction yards on the body, so every build runs at the 10% floor: a 4-tick base takes 40+ ticks (ten years at a quarterly tick).

RULINGS (Ben, 2026-09-23, form):
- Sourcing: restore BL-1003 (pools per market). This item requires it.
- Site multiplier: it stretches MATERIALS AND CASH as well as time, and that is PRICED AT PLACEMENT — the affordability gate, the Build door's capex preview and the rival scorer price cost x the site multiplier (PRODUCTION.md § Construction site time).
- Capacity: IN SCOPE here. Either the charter web charters a yard the player's catchment reaches, or the opening corp carries capacity; choose by measurement once BL-1003 has landed, since pools per market move where capacity sits.

PLUS THE FIXTURE: scripts/verify/lib.lua must place near the player's own works (not raster-first) and wait out the 12-tick tech gate, and its error must say 'stalled' when progress stops rather than 'never completed within 40 ticks'.

DONE WHEN. On every library seed, the seated player can place AND complete a military base in its home catchment within the fixture's bound; the affordability gate refuses a site whose multiplied cost the corp cannot meet; and scripts/verify/lib.lua stages on a pristine world.

ROUND 2 (2026-09-23, after BL-1003 merged; traces in that session scratchpad). With pools per market the build want reaches its own market (demand 8.75, steel priced 161) and convoys dispatch, but the base still stalled: (i) ~3,000 steel, nearly all the body pooled, sat in NINE BL-910 capital markets with base price 0 — never listed; (ii) the shortfall dispatcher ran at the top of the tick and credited arrivals at its end, so every delivery was re-exported before any clearing saw it (995 steel dispatches in 100 ticks into one market); (iii) with capacity stocked by hand the base ran at full rate and then starved for steel, so capacity is necessary but not sufficient.

RULINGS (Ben, 2026-09-23): capital markets are PRICED, at a premium over the carve (MARKETS.md; the size is NR-916) — this absorbs the sprint 46 draft CAPITAL_MARKET_SHELLS, whose census-then-choose plan the ruling replaces; and the tick order is advance -> arrivals -> economy -> clearing -> dispatch (SUPPLY.md § Dispatch trigger, one beat per haul). The goods-vs-force LP priority that reorder flips is NR-917.

ROUND 3 (2026-09-23, after BL-995 merged f274a3d5). Trade is now real world-wide (haulage_measure --far-trade, 4 seeds: 3,712 units sold at destinations in year one, 82.5% of it past the seller’s nearest market). The base still stalls, and the trace says why: STEEL PRODUCTION ON THE BODY COLLAPSES — listed steel 234/tick at tick 1, 75 by tick 5, 0 from ~tick 9 in every market — while unmet steel demand climbs 0 -> 341/tick; and the ~3,460 steel of opening stock was sold to the SHELVES at tick 1 (before any price gap existed), where it belongs to no one and never moves. With capacity stocked by hand the base runs at full rate and starves the moment its local shelf empties. Open: (1) why the shipped world stops making steel within ~9 ticks; (2) whether shelf stock should ever move (a merchant buying low and hauling — the option passed over for BL-995); (3) construction capacity, a TRANSMITTED good (road network, like power), so its reach is a wiring question — the earlier '0 yards' reading was a probe miscount by type name.

WORLD RULED (Ben, 2026-09-24, option B): BL-1066's done-when is taken on the FLIPPED world — after BL-1047 (epoch flip gates), on the 1960 world the player is actually handed — not on the epoch-0 verify world every reading so far was taken on (steel_chain_probe found epoch 0 is the ancient band with no steel makers at all; its anachronisms are BL-1070). Epoch 0 stays a supported start (Ben, same day).

CARRIED 2026-09-24: sprint 46 closed early; unscheduled pending the sprint 47 cut.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-24, a way to stimulate steel); Claude (written into POPULATION.md)
items.title: Population centres keep a housing stock standing, and its upkeep is an era-banded materials draw that includes steel
items.design:
SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-24). POPULATION.md § Housing owns the rule. Filed into sprint 46 on Ben's call though it is not a perfect fit for a sprint about wiring the generation into the game — it answers BL-1066's steel finding (the industrial band's iron ore and steel have almost no genuine buyer).

THE WORK. (1) A per-centre housing stock sized to population, wearing at an authored rate. (2) The upkeep and growth draw registered as WANT on the catchment market — the household path in market_clearing.cpp is the model; it must bid (MARKETS.md property 3) — with an era-banded basket authored in economy.lua (ancient: timber, stone, clay, planks; industrial: steel, dressed stone, ceramics). (3) Housing condition below full caps growth and lowers habitability, recovers with supply, never destroys (dim, never dark). (4) The condition is persistent state: save seam and state hash in the same commit. (5) Surfaced where a centre's habitability is read, with its cause.

MEASURE on the flipped 1960 world (BL-1047) with demand_census: steel's genuine demand before and after, and that the draw does not collapse habitability world-wide on tick 0 (ship the shape inert or ramped if the supply is not there yet — PRODUCTION.md's corollary for authoring).

DONE WHEN. On the flipped world, industrial centres bid steel for housing, steel makers are induced by it, and no centre's condition sits at its floor for want of a good its band cannot make.

items.author: Claude (steel_chain_probe, 2026-09-24); Ben (epoch 0 stays supported, 2026-09-24)

(2) ERAS.md decides whether an ancient firm may open a petroleum, coal or rare-earth mine at all; if not, the era band refuses it at the door (building_available / the recipe band), not the scorer. items.author: Ben (2026-09-24: goods should move); Claude
items.title: Stock on a market's shelf can move to a better market; today it belongs to no one and never leaves
items.design:
MECHANISM RULED (Ben, 2026-09-24): option (b) — the market exports its own surplus shelf stock by the net-price rule, the haul paid from the export. SUPPLY.md § Dispatch trigger ('A market exports its own shelf') owns it.

THE WORK. In the dispatch step, AFTER corporations' dispatch: for each market and good, shelf inventory (above what its own local consumers drew last clear — measure, do not guess) is a source under net(d) = price_d - haul - [handling, duty when built]; send to argmax net(d) above the margin, quantity = the same absorbable room corporations use (all pending subtracted). The convoy has no corporation: model its owner as the source market (a convoy field or a sentinel owner) and settle: on arrival the cargo lands on the DESTINATION market's shelf and sells there; the haul is charged against the export's proceeds — decide with FINANCE.md where the net proceeds go (the source market holds no treasury today: the options are that they vanish as the market's margin, or credit the source market's nation as a tariff-like line) and state it. Interdiction, LP and the arrived-this-tick rule apply as to any convoy. Harness rows: a shelf with a far better-priced market exports; one under the margin does not; no churn; goods conserved (shelf debit = cargo = destination shelf credit).

DONE WHEN. On the epoch-0 verify world the stranded shelf steel moves toward the markets pricing it (steel_chain_probe's shelf geography), and haulage_measure --far-trade shows market exports as their own line.

--- EARLIER ---
RULED IN DIRECTION (Ben, 2026-09-24: 'goods should move'); the MECHANISM is open. FOUND on BL-1066: auto-surplus sells every unit above processor reservation to the local market (the market is buyer of last resort), and market inventory has no owner, so nothing hauls it — on the epoch-0 verify world ~3,300 steel sat on 13 of 255 shelves while construction sites elsewhere paused for it. BL-995 (trade reaches for price) makes a SELLER haul before it sells; stock already on a shelf still cannot move.

MECHANISM OPTIONS (Ben's call, then written into SUPPLY.md and MARKETS.md): (a) any corporation may BUY shelf stock at the shelf's price and haul it under the same net-price rule — a merchant is just a corp acting on a gap, one rule for every corp; (b) the market itself exports its surplus shelf stock by the net-price rule, the haul paid from the sale; (c) a construction site or processor may buy from the nearest stocked shelf across markets, paying the haul (narrow: fixes consumers, not trade).

DONE WHEN. A shelf holding a good that another market prices above landed cost is drawn down by hauls, measured by haulage_measure --far-trade and steel_chain_probe's shelf geography.

CARRIED 2026-09-24: sprint 46 closed early; unscheduled pending the sprint 47 cut.

BEN (2026-09-24, the sprint 47 form): should the Logistic Point cap brake market exports this hard (about 46 of 3,300 stranded steel moved in 20 ticks) — 'measure more first'. A market export moves no money, the haul is the margin given up — CONFIRMED. The next reading is owed on the flipped world before any cap change.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-24, the sprint 47 design form); Claude
items.title: The world is built once at the Life gate, with its deposits, and moves forward through every wizard round instead of being rebuilt
items.design:
CARRIED TO SPRINT 48 (Ben, 2026-09-25, the sprint-47 close form): sprint 47 closes on the identity wave and its flair; this item opens sprint 48. NR-936 rides with it: the wizard's Next press does not wait for the running round, so a fast player can have rounds 3-6 building at once; with one world moved forward, round N+1 cannot start before round N lands, so decide here whether Next waits.

RULED (Ben, 2026-09-24: "move the whole half-built world"; "we don't want to do the work twice, so seed actual materials at the Life gate and pass tiles through the whole phase"; docs/development/drafts/sprint-47-rulings.md R1, R2).

WHY. Every lapse round's worker runs make_hard_coded_world from params to its own stop (startup_screens.cpp:375-379): stages 0-7 (Helios, Cinder, the Kepler chain, tiles with deposits, rivers, creeds, settlement) run again on every seam, and round 5 re-runs Empires, round 6 re-runs Empires and Exploration (hard_coded_world.cpp:550-916, :1158, :1313, :1497). Rounds 0-1 build a scratch world for the globe and discard it. Deposits already land at stage 4 (tile_generation.cpp Pass 6, generate_life_deposits_over :2284-2298), downstream of S8 Legacy and S9 Spend (planetology.cpp:1533-1555), so the ruling changes OWNERSHIP, not pass order.

THE WORK. (1) make_hard_coded_world becomes the composition of resumable stage functions over one generation_cursor carrying what the tail reads as locals today (world, report, naming, rw, deposit_scalar, kepler_tiles/pl/hist/creeds/settlement/np/corridors/grudges/region_polity/polity_treasuries/capital_market_shells, the last span's resume struct): gen_life_gate (bumps 0-5), gen_culture (:826-1138), gen_empires (:1158-1300), gen_exploration (:1313-1470), gen_industrialisation (:1488-1640) then the tail (bumps 9-12). The composition is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the monolith: every harness, fixture, gen_step_costs and the 16 seed-library pins keep one invocation. The stop_after_* flags stop being early returns and become 'run the composition up to stage N'. (2) The wizard: the Life round builds the REAL Life-gate world into slot 0 (the globe rasters pack off it; a planetology move relaunches it and drops every slot below); launch_wizard_history_run(i) takes slot i-1 and runs only stage i into slot i; invalidate_wizard_rounds_below(r) drops every slot below r and stale-marks in-flight ones (a stale landing drops record AND world, the pattern at startup_screens.cpp:439-449); Begin adopts slot 3 exactly as BL-1073 does. (3) The reroll path (delegated reading, NEEDS_REVIEW): the predecessor's closed world is HELD by a faithful copy at landing (BL-1034; world_copy_determinism proves a copy ticks as its original) and a copy is moved into the worker; a reroll re-copies; when the predecessor is not held, REPLAY from the Life gate with the fixed per-span seeds — bit-identical by determinism, ~0.5 s + 1.6 s + 1.5 s in Release (hard_coded_world.cpp:360-398). Measure the copy cost first (Rule 0b); if it exceeds the replay it saves, ship pure replay. Back keeps every record and world. (4) The gate world is Helios + Cinder + Kepler; Selene and Pallas stay in Finishing (an entity-id shift for two bodies no round shows — NEEDS_REVIEW). (5) Round 6 starts playing at the tap's final publish (history_sim.cpp:7899; the record is whole there); landing only swaps the world slot; poll_wizard_history_tap's snapshot path and the landed path must not fight over m_wiz_history[3]. (6) Proof: world_determinism twice; a cursor-vs-monolith check (owner_changes, polities, world digest) at EVERY round boundary on the 16 curated seeds, extending run_autostart_adopt's round-6 proof; begin_adopts_check.js green.

DONE WHEN (live). Press Next on rounds 4 and 5: the wait caption never names an earlier span ('Running the ancient era' never appears on round 5) and the elapsed count is shorter by the predecessor's measured cost; Back then Next on any round recomputes nothing; reroll round 5 and it opens on round 4's exact 1200 frame. Harness: the resumed build equals the monolithic build on the 16 seeds; digests unchanged.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-24, the sprint 47 design form); Claude
items.title: The landscape search runs inside generation at the companies stage, so markets carve on the searched roster and no world-gen roster is laid then removed

items.design:

NATION_GENERATION.md § Pass 5 — Naming rules a region is <People> <Region> with both halves native and the region word positional; a span founding must coin from the people half and its own position, never from the parent's finished string.

THE WORK. Find the span-founding name path (history_sim.cpp settle → the region name coin) and give it the people half + the region's own positional word, as settlement.cpp coins a migration founding; a harness row asserting no region name repeats its final word.

DONE WHEN. On the 16 curated seeds no region name ends in a doubled word; the seat card's HQ line reads one quarter word.

items.author: Claude (2026-09-25, lane F2 fix round, handed to the main session to file)
items.title: A tie or treaty standing at the 1660 seam draws on the Industrialisation round: the resumed span restates its standing links at its open
items.design:
FILED 2026-09-25 (found by lane F2's cold review; documented as a known gap in history_lapse.hpp's fleets-and-ties layer comment). Not in sprint 47.

THE GAP. The fleets-and-ties bake (BL-1095) opens a tie on subject_bound / province_bought and an arc on treaty_formed, and closes them on subject_freed / treaty_broken / realm_ended, in one forward walk over ONE record. The Industrialisation span copies exploration_upkeep_enabled and so keeps running the subjection and treaty blocks -- but a link bound before 1660 has its opening kind on the Exploration record and only its closing kind on the Industrialisation one, so round 6 finds a close with no open and draws nothing for it; hulls, harbours and sails are whole (they read the span's own samples and kinds). The same shape BL-1088 met for a realm's founding and answered with the `inherited` kind (20).

THE WORK. At a resumed span's open, the sim emits one record-only restatement per standing subject link and per standing treaty -- either the existing `inherited` kind with `other` naming what is restated, or two kinds of their own (`tie_inherited`, `treaty_inherited`) numbered past 24 -- carrying the overlord/subject pair (or the treaty pair and its remaining term) so the bake can open the segment at the span's first year. Gated exactly as the closing kinds are; the f=0 control byte-identical; in the next envelope bump. The bake's walk then needs no change beyond opening on the new kind(s); fleets_and_ties.lua gains a round-6 assertion that a tie standing at 1660 on the reference world draws at 1660 + one window.

DONE WHEN. On round 6 of the reference world the ties and arcs that stood at the close of round 5 are drawn from the first frame, and every one of them ends where the Industrialisation record ends it.

items.author: Claude (2026-09-25, lane BL-1049's open question, handed to the main session to file)
items.title: world_determinism's deep digest folds the history log and the record tables, so a world whose biography changed no longer digests identically
items.design:
FILED 2026-09-25. Not in sprint 47.

THE GAP. world_determinism builds its worlds with make_hard_coded_world alone, on which world::history_log is never seeded (seed_genesis_history runs in finish_campaign_world), and its deep digest folds no record table -- so BL-1049, which drops duplicate civilisation coinings and five lines of the prose history on the reference world, moved none of the harness's four digests. The player_seed_sweep digests (D_land onward) did move. A determinism harness that cannot see a change to the world's own biography is blind to one whole class of generation change.

THE WORK. Fold into the deep digest (a) the world's history log after seed_genesis_history (run the finish's genesis step on the harness world, or fold the generation_report's per-body dated history directly), and (b) the civilisation and universal-creed tables and the polity-name / civilisation-name / creed-name tables the records carry, in index order. Record the moved digits old -> new with the change (a re-bless of the harness's own row only; the sweep pins do not move). DONE WHEN: a one-line change to a civilisation name on the reference world moves seedA/on; the harness still reads bit-identical run to run.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-25, the sprint-47 close form); filed by Claude
items.title: Settle tick 1 costs 44-62 s against ~1.5 s for the other eleven: instrument it by phase and hand the cause to the economy lane
items.design:
FILED 2026-09-25 from NR-932 (Ben: C, both; the progress tap is sprint 47's, this is the other half). Not in sprint 47.

THE READING. Inside the twelve-tick settle in round 6's worker, tick 1 runs 44-62 s (seed 0: settle 113,922 ms, tick 1 56,881 ms; seed 28: 68,832 ms) while ticks 2-12 cost ~1.5 s each.

FIRST READING (2026-09-25, gen_step_costs --finish 0, Release, the lap timing now printed by finish_campaign_world): settle 55,962 ms; slowest tick 1 at 38,487 ms, of which run_economy_step 38,453 ms (lap 1: the economy step and dispatch), clear_markets 24, apply_budget+nation_step 9, the other three 0. So the cost is inside run_economy_step on econ step 1 -- the corp AI cadence (half the slots per step) is the first suspect, not a cold pool. Seed 28 not yet read.

THE WORK. Time tick 1 by phase (the first clearing over cold pools? the first dispatch?) on seeds 0 and 28 in Release, record the split here, and file the fix against the owning economy work -- NR-915 (the tick tail) may already own the cause. Measure, do not reshape.

DONE WHEN. The phase that costs tick 1 is named with its milliseconds on two seeds and the fix is filed where it belongs.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-25, the round-feedback form after the sprint-47 live clicks); filed by Claude
items.title: Roads are a tree plus a detour test, and only villages above a size spur: no lattice, and round 6's tail inside 35 s
items.design:
FILED 2026-09-25 (Ben, walking round 6: "we also need many fewer roads... it should be heavily discouraged to build a lattice of roads"; he chose the tree plus a detour test over "no second path", and spurs only for villages above a size). LOGISTICS.md § 4 carries the rule; STARTUP.md § Round 6 carries the 35 s target.

THE WORK. (1) Replace the relative-neighbour redundancy edges with the DETOUR TEST: after the Kruskal MST, a candidate link between two centres is laid only when the network's route between them costs more than 2x the direct A* route (one constant, named). The percentile rationing of loops applies to the loops the test admits (a delegated reading that keeps BL-618/BL-621 intact; Ben may overturn). (2) A village lays a spur only above a size floor, MEASURED on the 16 curated seeds first (Rule 0b: road tiles, spur count and pass time per floor candidate). (3) The border link rule is unchanged.

A WORLD-MOVER: every road digest and the sweep pins move -- read road tile counts, pass time (gen_step_costs --finish) and the haulage baseline (memory: goldens cannot see trade) on the 16 seeds before and after, then ONE re-bless.

DONE WHEN. No lattice on a capture of the densest seed; road pass time and tile count recorded old -> new per seed; round 6's tail lands within 35 s of arrival on seeds 0 and 28 in Release (gen_step_costs); one re-bless; road_generation_harness green (connectivity held).

A sim beat: it moves sea legs, lanes, displacement and every pin -- read on the 16 seeds first, one re-bless. Pairs with BL-1115 (sea legs in the later spans), which should land first so currents act on legs that run.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-25, the round-feedback form after the sprint-47 live clicks); filed by Claude
items.title: Measure the tribute subjects pay their overlords on the 16 seeds, then show it running home along the ties on the Exploration round
items.design:
FILED 2026-09-25 (Ben: "what we don't see, but really should, is the colonial conquest of smaller nations, exploiting them to bring wealth back to larger polities"; he chose A -- measure, then show what the sim has, before any new mechanism). EXPLORATION.md § What a treaty is: tribute is already a remittance from subject to overlord.

THE WORK. (1) READ FIRST (Rule 0b): on the 16 curated seeds, how many subjects stand overseas vs home, how much tribute flows per round and to whom, and how often a large polity subjects a small one across water -- a column in exploration_sweep. (2) If the flow is there, draw it: tribute running subject -> overlord along the tie, weighted by the amount, on round 5. (3) If it is not there, that is the finding: report it and the colonial-drive mechanism becomes its own call for Ben (the B he did not pick yet).

DONE WHEN. The reading recorded per seed; the flow drawn where it exists; Ben's live click.

items.author: Ben (the delegated-decision form, 2026-09-25); filed by Claude
items.title: Firms are chartered in the Industrialisation span when a region's stock crosses the running price, with the points debited
items.design:
FILED 2026-09-25 from NR-925 (Ben: B, real in-span chartering, overturning the record-only reading). INDUSTRIALISATION.md § Beat 1 — Industry: cities make industry points (Firms are chartered in the span).

THE SHIFT. Today the span only NOTES works_chartered crossings (record-only, f = 2) and the firms are chartered at the 1960 close from each city's budget, dated by pairing. Ruled: the crossing IS the charter -- the firm exists from that year and the points are debited.

OPEN DESIGN (a design pass first): (1) how the close's charter budget (BL-1032, the charter budget seam) and the landscape search reconcile with firms already chartered -- the search re-scores a fixed roster or charters only the remainder; (2) whether an in-span firm acts in the span or waits for 1960 (acting is a far larger beat); (3) the dawn cluster NR-940 accepted -- at the running price most crossings land 1660-1760, so most firms would be founded early; re-read with the debit in place, since a debit slows the next crossing; (4) the seat briefing's founding year becomes the charter year itself (no pairing).

A WORLD-MOVER with its own re-bless: read firm counts, founding-year spread and treasury on the 16 seeds before and after (Rule 0b); tune nothing to make a seed behave.

THE WORK. (1) Derive each nation's band at the 1960 fold from the realm it grew from (roster_band_for_capacity) -- DELEGATED READING: "the realm it grew from" rather than any realm folded into the nation; Ben may overturn. (2) Persist it on nation_component (a world save bump) and retire the world-wide world::campaign_band. (3) Make the registry actor-aware: every consumer of the band -- the browse roster, construction validity, the recipe pass, corp_ai's build choices, --serve/MCP validation -- asks for the acting corporation's nation's band. (4) The Industry mask (BL-1109) still seeds earned_techs within a band.

READ FIRST (Rule 0b): per seed, how many nations derive ancient -- NR-934 found every library seed industrial at WORLD grain, which says nothing of the spread per nation.

DONE WHEN. Two nations on one world can open on different bands; a firm in an ancient nation is refused an industrial building through every front door (UI, command, MCP); save round trip carries the per-nation band; one re-bless if any digest moves.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-25, second live look at the sprint-47 build); filed by Claude

The record is built and the lane draws (sea_lanes.lua, seed 32: 16 lanes), first as a thin dashed line that hid under the colonial ties, then as a wide soft sea-blue band under them -- and the band was still not clearly seen at the live app.

WHY IT HIDES. The tribute leg writes most lane uses (seed 46: 619 of 663), so almost every lane runs the same capital-to-capital line as its tie, and the lanes open late in the span.

THE WORK, with BL-1118 (round legends) beside it: the legend names the lane; the lane gets a form of its own that reads at a glance (candidates: a brighter core line inside the band, a shipping-route glyph at each end, or an arc bowed away from the tie). Once BL-1115 (sea legs in the later spans) lands, wet campaigns write lanes off the ties too -- read how many before choosing.

DONE WHEN. Ben finds a lane at the live app without a pointer.
